trust_decision.summary: Whether a dotted code reference from an (uploadable) agent YAML config may be imported and used as a tool/callback/schema/model/agent class is decided by a top-level-module denylist in _validate_module_reference; the denylist omitted exec-capable stdlib modules (cProfile, timeit, trace, ...).

landing_point.why: The summary names agent-config code injection; the only blocking logic for code references is the _BLOCKED_MODULES denylist and _validate_module_reference right below it.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /dev/apps/{app_name}/builder/save (adk web) uploading root_agent.yaml, then agent load via AgentLoader._load_from_yaml_config -> from_config
fix_sites.module_kind: core library (agent config resolution), denylist constant

fix_sites.entry_point: same; also public API resolve_code_reference / resolve_fully_qualified_name / LlmAgent._resolve_tools

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Every config-driven import already funnels through _validate_module_reference (resolve_fully_qualified_name, _resolve_agent_code_reference, resolve_code_reference, LlmAgent._resolve_tools), so a solver who extends the denylist has nothing else to dismiss; the only arguable remainder is third-party exec-capable packages, which the fix itself deliberately keeps resolvable.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Third-party integration references (e.g. pydantic.BaseModel, langchain/crewai tools) and google.adk / agent-package references must stay resolvable; an allowlist-to-own-package-only or 'block everything with a dot' fix breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: top-level stdlib module names present in sys.stdlib_module_names (cProfile, timeit, trace, pydoc, doctest, bdb, py_compile)
modules removed from the stdlib but still importable via shims/backports (distutils, pipes, telnetlib, imp, ...)
harmless-looking stdlib modules (json, base64, operator) blocked by design

O8b_injection_room.sibling: _get_class_from_string imports a dotted class path from services.yaml with no _validate_module_reference call
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: services.yaml is another YAML config naming classes by dotted path; a maintainer could plausibly route it through the same denylist or forget it. In our copy it could be made loadable from the app dir (builder accepts .yaml).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: custom metric function path imported and called without the module-reference check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same dotted-name-to-callable pattern from a config (eval_config custom_metrics code_config.name, eval_config.py:266-269); today it is developer-authored JSON, a sibling would make it reachable from an uploaded/recorded file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: _import_plugin_object resolves extra plugin dotted names without the check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugins are named by dotted path like tools; a config-driven plugin list would be a natural extension.

O9_family: Code injection via config-driven dynamic import (incomplete denylist, CWE-184)

O10_build.toolchain: pip/uv install of google-adk with test extras; pytest

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add cProfile (and maybe timeit/trace) to _BLOCKED_MODULES, i.e. extend the enumerated denylist instead of blocking the whole stdlib plus the dropped-module and test-package names.

out_of_scope_notes: Third-party exec-capable packages (e.g. pytest itself, installed in the affected configuration) remain resolvable after the fix by design; not pursued.
services.yaml under agents_dir is loaded at startup and is not writable through the builder upload (writes go under agents_dir/app_name); not pursued.
POST /dev/apps/{app_name}/tests/run (src/google/adk/cli/dev_server.py:685-736) is the replay trigger that requires pytest; it is the execution step, not a resolution route.
